<issue identifier="MM-479">
<title>Passwordless accounts: rework deleteAccount to email-token-or-wallet-signature</title>
<description>
Part of Phase 1 of `docs/design-plans/2026-07-12-passwordless-auth.md`. Split out of the optional-password-at-creation work so that lands independently.

## Why

An account with a NULL `password_hash` **cannot be deleted**. `crates/pds/src/routes/delete_account.rs` verifies the account password before consuming the single-use email token, and the no-password case is folded into the generic credential failure:

```rust
// crates/pds/src/routes/delete_account.rs (~line 76)
// No such account, or a mobile account with no main password: nothing to verify against.
```

which returns 401. The wallet inherits this: `confirm_identity_removal` in `apps/identity-wallet/src-tauri/src/identity_removal.rs` (~line 475) takes `password` + emailed `token` and calls `delete_account` first, so a passwordless identity dead-ends at the credential check with everything intact and no path forward.

Today this is latent — every account has a password. It becomes reachable the moment `accounts.password_optional` ships, which is why that flag must not reach a public beta before this does: it would mint accounts the holder can never remove.

## Shape

Keep the two-factor shape (something you hold + something you control), swapping the password factor for a device-key signature when the account has no password:

* **Passworded account** — unchanged. Password + email token.
* **Passwordless account** — email token + a device-key-signed canonical envelope in the `sovereign_session.rs` / `verify_admin_device_request` mold: domain-versioned string binding server DID, account DID, signing key, the delete intent, timestamp, nonce; verified against the authoritative current PLC `rotationKeys` (never the cached DID doc); nonce anti-replay.
* Preserve the existing oracle discipline — the failure for "unknown DID", "wrong password", and "bad signature" must stay uniform, so the endpoint never becomes an account-existence or credential-shape oracle (see the comment at `delete_account.rs:37`).
* Verify the credential factor **before** consuming the single-use email token, as today, so a bad signature never burns the token.

## Wallet

* `confirm_identity_removal` takes an optional password; when the identity's host advertises the optional-password capability and the account has none, sign the removal envelope instead.
* `RemovalError::InvalidCredentials` copy currently says "invalid password or confirmation code" — needs a passwordless variant.
* The removal flow already runs a biometric gate and a passwordless unlock (`RemovalError` carries a needs-unlock variant); reuse it rather than adding a second prompt.

## Acceptance criteria

* An account created with no password can be fully removed from the wallet: `deleteAccount` succeeds, the tombstone is written, local state is wiped.
* A replayed removal envelope is refused (nonce anti-replay), and an envelope for DID A cannot delete DID B.
* Unknown DID, wrong password, and bad signature remain indistinguishable to the caller.
* A wrong credential does not consume the email token.
* Passworded accounts keep working unchanged, including migrated-in accounts that arrived with a password.
* Bruno collection updated for any body/shape change (`just bruno-check` checks paths only — the body change relies on the manual rule in AGENTS.md).
</description>

<title>Passwordless auth: retire the account password in favor of device-key/passkey factors</title>
<description>
Follow-up to the passwordless design exploration captured in `docs/design-plans/2026-07-12-passwordless-auth.md` (branch `claude/passwordless-login-bc4umw`).

## Why

The password is already a second-class credential in this architecture: the wallet logs in via OAuth+DPoP and retains no password, the root of trust is the Secure-Enclave device key holding `rotationKeys[0]`, `accounts.password_hash` has been nullable since V008, and `createSession` already falls through to app-password verification for accounts with a NULL main password. Meanwhile password reset is dead in practice (outbound email is stubbed, <issue id="fbeb902e-c32b-400a-af47-37eccd58d65b" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-211/outbound-email-delivery-email-confirmationupdate-endpoints">MM-211</issue>), so the password is an unrecoverable liability posing as a recovery factor. Identity recovery never depended on it — that's the device key's 2-of-3 Shamir split.

## What the password still gates (the actual work)

1. **OAuth consent** (`oauth_authorize.rs`) — the wallet's own login path; a NULL-hash account cannot pass consent today. Needs a device-key-signed or passkey (WebAuthn) factor. The signed-envelope verification pattern already exists for admin-companion devices (`auth/guards.rs::verify_admin_device_request`).
2. **Account creation** — non-empty password required in `/v1/dids` and `createAccount` new-account mode; make optional (migration mode already stores NULL).
3. `deleteAccount` — password + email token in body; rework to email-token-or-wallet-signature for passwordless accounts.
4. Third-party clients (Bluesky app, goat) keep working via **app passwords** minted in the wallet — zero server changes needed.

## Phasing (from the design plan)

* **Phase 1:** optional password at creation; device-key/passkey factor on OAuth consent; `deleteAccount` rework. Keep interop endpoints (password branch of `createSession`, standard `createAccount`) for migrated-in accounts.
* **Phase 2:** cross-device login approval — QR-scan (wallet-initiated, phishing-resistant) first; **push-to-approve** later, once the E2E-encrypted notification relay lands (<pull-request id="34230e45-6259-4c9a-b58d-6b135adf84e3" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/review/design-exploration-e2e-encrypted-notification-relay-for-self-hosted-327f880332d1">malpercio-dev/ezpds#207</pull-request>, `docs/design-plans/2026-07-10-notification-relay.md`). Push-approve needs MFA-fatigue mitigations (origin display, number matching).
* **Hard prerequisite (parallel):** the Shamir reconstruction ceremony (or iCloud-synced passkeys), so a lost device is not a total PDS lockout before the password escape hatch is removed.

## Definition of done (exploration → plan promotion)

* Full design plan with acceptance criteria promoted from the exploration doc
* Decision recorded: passkey/WebAuthn vs device-key-signed consent as the primary factor
* Recovery-ceremony dependency scheduled ahead of any password removal
</description>

# Linear Development Workflow

This skill manages the full lifecycle of working on a Linear issue: from picking it up through opening a PR.

## Starting Work on an Issue

When the user indicates they want to work on a Linear issue (e.g., "Let's work on MM-42"):

1. **Parse the issue identifier** from the user's message. The pattern is `MM-` followed by a number.

2. **Fetch the issue details** from Linear using the `get_issue` tool with the parsed identifier. Display a brief summary to the user: title, description (truncated if long), priority, and any existing labels.

3. **Update the issue in Linear:**
   - Set the status to **"In Progress"**
   - Assign it to **"me"** (the authenticated user)

   Use the `save_issue` tool with the issue's `id`, `state: "In Progress"`, and `assignee: "me"`.

4. **Create a git branch from a fresh base** using the issue's suggested branch name:
   - The `get_issue` response includes a `branchName` field — use that as the branch name.
   - **Fetch first, then branch from the remote tip — never from a possibly-stale local HEAD:**
     `git fetch origin main && git checkout -b <branchName> origin/main`
     A stale base silently duplicates work that already merged (hours lost rebuilding an already-shipped backend is the known failure mode).
   - If the branch already exists locally, check it out, then run `git log --oneline <branchName>..origin/main` and surface to the user how far behind the base is.

5. **Verify sibling work is in the base.** If the issue depends on or overlaps sibling issues already marked Done in Linear, confirm their PRs are actually present in the branch base (e.g. `git log --oneline origin/main | grep -i mm-nnn`, or check for the files/routes they added) before concluding any related feature is "missing". **"Linear says Done but the code isn't here" is a hard stop-and-verify signal — it almost always means your base is stale, not that the feature needs building.**

6. **Confirm to the user** what happened: issue assigned, status updated, branch created/checked out (and from which base commit). Then ask what they'd like to tackle first, or summarize the issue so they can dive in.

## Opening a PR (Auto-transition to "In Review")

When the user asks to open a PR, create a pull request, or you detect that a PR is being created for a branch associated with a Linear issue:

1. **Identify the Linear issue** from the current branch name. Linear branch names typically contain the issue identifier (e.g., `malpercio/mm-42-fix-the-thing`). Extract the `MM-XXX` portion.

2. **Create the PR** as the user requests (follow normal PR creation workflow).

3. **After the PR is successfully created**, update the Linear issue:
   - Set the status to **"In Review"**
   - Attach the PR URL as a link on the issue using the `links` field in `save_issue`

   Use `save_issue` with the issue's `id`, `state: "In Review"`, and `links: [{"url": "<pr-url>", "title": "Pull Request"}]`.

4. **Confirm** to the user that the issue has been moved to "In Review" and the PR link has been attached.

## Important Notes

- Always fetch the issue first to confirm it exists and get the full `id` (UUID) needed for updates.
- If the issue is already "In Progress" and assigned, skip those updates and just create the branch.
- If branch creation fails (e.g., uncommitted changes), inform the user and suggest next steps rather than silently failing.
- The PR-to-"In Review" transition should happen automatically whenever a PR is opened during a session where the user started work on a Linear issue. Track the active issue identifier throughout the session.

### `optionalPassword`

An account can be created on this server with no password at all. A client that
sees this capability may omit the password field entirely when creating an
account; the account is stored with no password hash and authenticates
afterwards through its device key — wallet-confirmed OAuth consent and sovereign
sessions — plus app passwords for standard AT Protocol clients like the Bluesky
app.

Passwordless accounts are not a new storage shape: accounts that migrate in from
another server have always been stored without a password. What this capability
changes is only whether a *new* account may be created that way.

An **empty** password is refused whether or not this is enabled, and that is
deliberate: an empty string is what an uninitialised form field sends, so
accepting one would let a client bug create an account with no credential that
nobody asked for. Omitting the field is the only way to ask.

**Controlled by:** `accounts.password_optional`. Off by default — a passwordless
account depends on device-key custody you cannot verify on the account holder's
behalf, so a deployment whose users are not all running the identity wallet
should keep the password required. Enable it with `[accounts] password_optional =
true` (`EZPDS_ACCOUNTS_PASSWORD_OPTIONAL`) and the capability appears. Turning it
back off stops new passwordless accounts being created; it does not affect
accounts that already have no password, which keep working exactly as before.

### `didWebHosting`

Custos serves an opted-in account's `did:web` document at the account's own
domain (`/.well-known/did.json`) and emits an identity event so relays re-resolve
after an edit.

Hosting is opt-in **per account**, never automatic, and only ever for a domain
the user controls: moving the document onto Custos trades away some of the
independence a self-hosted document gives an identity, so it is the account
holder's decision. Exit is a DNS repoint away.

**Controlled by:** always. The server-side capability is inherent to running
Custos and has no operator switch; whether any given account uses it is that
account holder's choice.

### `waitlist`

A public interest-signup waitlist for a pre-launch deployment: an unauthenticated
`POST /waitlist` accepting an email address plus an optional atproto handle, meant
to be posted to directly from a marketing page on another origin (the endpoint is
CORS-open and carries no credentials). Signups are idempotent per email — a repeat
returns the same success and never discloses whether an address was already on the
list — and the handle is syntax-checked but deliberately never resolved, so the
endpoint has no outbound-request surface. The operator reads the list back with
`GET /v1/admin/waitlist` (newest first, with a total), which keeps working even
after the public endpoint is switched off again.

**Controlled by:** `waitlist.enabled`. Off by default — an instance that isn't
running a launch funnel should not carry a public write endpoint it never asked
for. Enable it with `[waitlist] enabled = true` (`EZPDS_WAITLIST_ENABLED`) and the
capability appears; the per-IP signup rate cap is `rate_limit.waitlist_per_5min`
(`EZPDS_RATE_LIMIT_WAITLIST_PER_5MIN`, default 30).

An account can be permanently deleted with a device-key-signed proof from one of

and honouring only the weaker one would make the endpoint answer differently

proofs remain one indistinguishable response.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Require a changelog fragment *added by the change itself* when a PR changes a shipped
# surface (fragments already sitting in changelog.d/ from other work don't satisfy it).
# CHANGELOG_BASE_REF is set to the PR base SHA in CI; an explicit first argument is
# convenient for local checks. With neither, fragment validity is still checked but
# presence is not required because there is no trustworthy comparison range.
set -euo pipefail

cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

base_ref="${1:-${CHANGELOG_BASE_REF:-}}"
fragment_dir="changelog.d"
fragment_re='^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*\.(added|changed|fixed|removed|security)\.md$'

fail=0
fragment_count=0
while IFS= read -r fragment; do
  name="${fragment##*/}"
  if ! [[ "$name" =~ $fragment_re ]]; then
    echo "✗ invalid changelog fragment '$fragment' — expected <id>.<added|changed|fixed|removed|security>.md" >&2
    fail=1
    continue
  fi
  if ! grep -q '[^[:space:]]' "$fragment"; then
    echo "✗ changelog fragment '$fragment' is empty" >&2
    fail=1
    continue
  fi
  fragment_count=$((fragment_count + 1))
done < <(find "$fragment_dir" -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '*.md' ! -name README.md | sort)

if [ "$fail" -ne 0 ]; then
  exit 1
fi

if [ -z "$base_ref" ]; then
  echo "✓ $fragment_count valid changelog fragment(s); no base ref supplied, so presence was not evaluated"
  exit 0
fi

# Batch PR Review-Comment Triage

Pull every unresolved review thread on the current PR in one command, then triage the batch. The user should never have to paste review comments one at a time.

## Fetch unresolved threads

Determine the PR number for the current branch (`gh pr view --json number -q .number`), then:

```bash
gh api graphql -f query='
query($owner:String!,$repo:String!,$pr:Int!){
  repository(owner:$owner,name:$repo){
    pullRequest(number:$pr){
      reviewThreads(first:100){
        nodes{
          isResolved isOutdated path line
          comments(first:30){nodes{author{login} body url}}
        }
      }
    }
  }
}' -F owner=<owner> -F repo=<repo> -F pr=<number> \
| jq '[.data.repository.pullRequest.reviewThreads.nodes[]
       | select(.isResolved==false)
       | {path, line, isOutdated,
          comments: [.comments.nodes[] | {author: .author.login, url, body}]}]'
```

Also fetch top-level (non-thread) review bodies and issue comments if the bot posts summaries there:

```bash
gh pr view <number> --json reviews,comments
```

## Triage the batch

For each unresolved thread, classify before fixing anything:

1. **Correctness / security / portability** — verify the claim against the actual code, then fix if real. Automated reviewers assert confidently and are sometimes wrong; refute with evidence when they are.
2. **Legitimate but out of scope** — file a follow-up issue rather than growing the PR.
3. **Pure style nit / preference** — decline with a one-line reason.

Present the full disposition table (thread → classification → action) to the user in ONE message before applying fixes, so they approve the batch rather than each item. Note that every fix-commit re-triggers CI and (for assertive bots like CodeRabbit) a fresh review round that tends to find one more micro-nit — batch fixes into a single commit where possible.

## Resolving threads

After pushing fixes, reply/resolve via:

```bash
gh api graphql -f query='mutation($id:ID!){resolveReviewThread(input:{threadId:$id}){thread{isResolved}}}' -F id=<threadId>
```

(Include `id` in the reviewThreads query above if you plan to resolve threads programmatically.)

the recorded request set instead, which is the only thing that witnesses the
absence of a call — confirmed non-vacuous by inverting it to expect 1 and
